requirement:
The initial request MUST provide the six tool definitions above and the
following prompt. The harness MUST replace `{{subject_kind}}` with `requirement`
or `example`, `{{subject_name}}` with the full subject name, and
`{{mandatory_inputs}}` with the complete mandatory inputs as a JSON array using
the existing evidence-input formats. The template MUST otherwise be used as
written. Its review guidance MUST follow {impl}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`,
{cite}`requirements.examples.evidence`, and {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.

```text
Bring your expert judgment to the task of assessing whether a project's sources satisfy a requirement or example.

Subject: {{subject_kind}} {{subject_name}}

Read the subject and mandatory inputs below. Use habeas to request any additional
source information you need. Use list_files to discover files and directories,
outline to list a file's selectable nodes, ripgrep to search file contents, and
references to list requirement names or
every source that references the selected definitions.
The harness records source inputs for you; listings and reference lookups are
not evidence.

Assess only the named subject, using cited requirements and definitions as context.
For a requirement, check that the code marked {impl} implements every obligation
completely and exactly as stated, and that tests cover the interesting points in
the design space, including relevant boundaries and failure cases. Also check that the
implementation is marked completely: code that implements part of the
requirement without an {impl} reference to it, including code that refers to it
only with {cite}, is a gap. So is behavior in the {impl} code that this
requirement does not specify, unless another definition that code implements
specifies it. When another requirement implements part of the subject, assess
whether its text carries out that part; do not reassess its implementation,
tests, or evidence. If there are no tests,
assess whether simplicity or impracticality justifies their absence, and explain.
For an example, assess whether test setup and assertions cover its scenario and
expected outcomes. A true judgment needs at least one {test} reference to the
example in the supplied inputs. Explain the coverage.

Choose true when the subject meets these criteria. Choose {"FIXME": ["..."]} when
the remaining gaps are explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests;
list their issue references or other identifying content. The usual convention
is FIXME(#125) or FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123), but references may occur elsewhere.
Choose false for other gaps or insufficient evidence. Explain your judgment in
a Markdown rationale with source locations, including any acknowledged gaps; for
a requirement, explain the implementation and testing judgments.

When you are ready, call submit_judgment exactly once with determination and
rationale. That tool call is your final answer.

Mandatory inputs:
{{mandatory_inputs}}
```
rationale:
## Judgment: `requirements.authoring.initial_prompt` is satisfied

### Implementation

- **Template source.** `prompt_template` (`src/authoring/mod.rs:614`) takes the prompt text straight from `md/requirements/authoring.md` with `include_str!`. It starts at the opening line, `DEFINITION_PROMPT`, and ends at the closing code fence. The template is therefore used "as written", and the book chapter is the only copy of the text. The opening line occurs only once in the chapter, inside this requirement's template, so the lookup cannot land on another prompt. The citation prompt's opening line is different.
- **Placeholder substitution.** `fill` (`mod.rs:628`) replaces `{{name}}` placeholders in a single pass. Substituted text that itself contains a placeholder, such as a requirement quoting a template, is left alone. Unknown `{{` sequences are copied through unchanged.
- **Subject kind.**
  - `initial_prompt` (`mod.rs:655`) fills `subject_kind` from `AssessmentKind::noun` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs:22`), which delegates to `DefinitionKind::noun` and yields `requirement` or `example`.
  - `subject_name` is the full subject name.
  - `mandatory_inputs` is `serde_json::to_string_pretty` of the mandatory input set. That set is an array of evidence-input values in the existing formats.
  - `DefinitionKind::noun` in `src/lib.rs` carries other `{impl}` markers but not this one. It is a general helper reached through the marked `AssessmentKind::noun`, so I do not count it as a gap.
- **Six tools.** `tool_definitions_with` (`mod.rs:754`) starts from `tools::definitions()` and adds `submit_judgment`. The tests confirm the model receives exactly the six tools `habeas`, `list_files`, `outline`, `references`, `ripgrep` and `submit_judgment`.
- **Delivery.** `assess` and `converse` build a `CompletionRequest` from this prompt plus the tools. Both the Ollama and Bedrock paths use it.
- **Review guidance.** The template text carries the review-criteria, example-evidence and outcome wording from the requirement. That wording is cited to `requirements.ci.review_criteria`, `requirements.examples.evidence` and `requirements.ci.outcomes`, and I did not reassess those requirements.
- **Marking.** The relevant functions all carry `{impl}`: `DEFINITION_PROMPT`, `prompt_template`, `fill`, `initial_prompt`, `tool_definitions_with`, `tool_definitions`, `assess` and `AssessmentKind::noun`. I found no unmarked code that implements part of the requirement, and no behaviour in the marked code that goes beyond it. The citation-prompt branch is covered by `requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`, which is also marked on those functions.

### Tests

- **`initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template`** (`tests/authoring_cli.rs:735`) is the main test.
  - It reads the template from the chapter and runs both a requirement subject and an example subject.
  - It checks that the `Subject: {kind} {name}` line is substituted correctly.
  - It checks that no `{{` remains.
  - It checks that the prompt starts and ends with the template text, so the template is otherwise unchanged.
  - It parses the rendered mandatory inputs as a JSON array. Each element must match exactly one evidence-input form with that form's fields.
  - It checks that the subject itself is present. For an example it also checks that the cited requirement is present, and for a requirement it checks that the terminology input is present.
- **`placeholders_are_filled_in_one_pass`** (`mod.rs:1974`) covers the single-pass boundary: a substituted `{{b}}` is not expanded again, and an unknown `{{c}}` is preserved.
- **The Ollama test** (`ollama_cli_delivers_sources_…`) asserts that the initial prompt contains the opening line, the requirement text, the definition, the implementation and test functions, and `submit_judgment exactly once`. It also asserts that the six tool names are sent.
- **The Bedrock test** asserts that the same prompt and the same six tools are sent, including the `submit_judgment` schema.
- **`agreeing_assessments_record_the_first`** also checks the opening line and tool set across conversations.

Together these cover both subject kinds, placeholder edge cases, both backends, the tool set, and the mandatory-input JSON format.

### Conclusion

The sources implement every obligation of the requirement and are marked completely. The tests cover the design space and no gaps are acknowledged, so the determination is `true`.

:::{req} evidence

Every defined example MUST have an `evidence/<full-example-name>.json` file whose `example` string exactly matches the current example body. A true determination MUST have at least one `{test}` reference to the example, covered by an evidence input. The reviewer MUST assess its tests under {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria` and use the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`; the no-test justification for a requirement MUST NOT establish a true example judgment. Habeas MUST apply the same missing-evidence, determination, input validation, and reference-coverage checks used for requirements. It MUST report a true determination with no test reference and changed example text with a compact line-oriented diff.
:::{req} outcomes
A requirement or example judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and source comments or tests
explicitly acknowledge those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the gaps and
their source locations in the rationale and record their issue references or
other identifying content from the inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. The expected source convention is
`FIXME(issue-number)`, for example `FIXME(#125)` or
`FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)`. References MAY appear elsewhere in the comment or
test; the reviewer MUST recognize explicit acknowledgments without requiring
that spelling. When no issue reference is present, the strings MUST identify the
documented gap using its source content. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in
recorded evidence inputs; a bare issue reference without an acknowledged gap
MUST NOT suffice.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
